label: early original-phase input of s/b/l/a/d
explanation: Token-identity unit in the original (input) phase: fires when the input token is one of s, b, l, a, d (rates 21-27% vs 5% base; weaker for w, k, m, very weak for v, i) and the step is early (t=0..3 carry ~95% of mass, peak at t=1, falling off sharply by t=4-5). Mostly first occurrences of the token (93% of mass). Nearly silent on the delimiter and copy phase (2% of mass; small blips when the model re-reads the trigger tokens). Magnitude is highest at t=1-3 after certain prefixes (e.g. 1 z / 1 e followed by s or b reach the max), so the preceding context modulates strength; whether a trigger token fires also depends on prior inputs (e.g. after another trigger token it is often suppressed), which the simple predicate misses. Extending to t=3 or adding w/k/m raises mass recall (to ~0.93) at the cost of precision.
